doc.title: Benny Powell interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 16, 1999 [interview 2 of 2]

title: Lecture-demonstrations and starting trombone at twelve
summary: He has given lecture-demonstrations for decades, and recalls taking up trombone at 12 with teacher Eddie Pearson and a boyhood band with Vernell Fournier.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Picking up the horn: first instrument and the trombone

blocks.x: For 35 years. I’ve done — or maybe 40 — I’ve done what’s called a lecture- demonstration. I think Billy Taylor started this in the 60s, where we lecture and we demonstrate. And I’ve been doing that constantly, every year, because for me it’s been like a commitment. Naturally education — I’ve done all these Broadway shows and Count Basie and all of that, and I realized that education is the key to it. Because when I first started playing trombone, I think maybe last time I told you when I was 12 years old I played drums when I was 9. When I was 12 years old I was sitting on a couch, I looked at the back of it, there was a trombone. As soon as I thought I wanted to play trombone, my mother found me a good teacher. I was 12. So I was able to become professional at 14 years the guy I studied with was Eddie Pearson. And I was a little egghead anyway. I found me and most of my friends, Vernell Fournier, we all grew up together. We had a kid’s band. I think we were 13 and 14, and we were working jobs. But it’s because we were never silly guys. You see studying music, or sports or whatever I guess, maybe music more so because it’s a kind of thought thing, you don’t have to run out there. Anyway, it makes you a little old man. Most of the guys I talk to, you know when we talked in retrospect, they were all little old men, just like my little nieces and stuff. The one that’s three years old is a little old spirit. Oh man, and you should see how naturally, when she’s playing the violin, and she’s in — I think some of it is because the teachers, she’s emulating a teacher. But man it sure looks like the real thing. She looks like Itzak Perlman to me.
It’s already a part of her.
